title: Bismuth/Yttria co-doped aluminosilicate fiber: impact of electron irradiation on optical properties
abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>We report on changes in absorptive, emissive and waveguiding properties of Bismuth doped yttria–aluminosilicate (Bi–Al–Y–Si) fiber under the action of high-energy electrons. In addition to the drastic rise of induced absorption in the fiber as a result of bombardment with electrons (measured by ∼800 dB m<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup> in the VIS range at the maximal irradiation dose of ∼200 KGy(SiO<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>) or 1 × 10<jats:sup>14</jats:sup> cm<jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>), we reveal prominent (∼20 fold at the maximal dose) growth of the fiber emissive potential in NIR (∼1.2 <jats:italic>µ</jats:italic>m) at its pumping in VIS (at 730 nm), an effect never reported before; both phenomena are inferred to arise due to strong growth of the content of Bi-related active centers, mostly of the Bi(Al) type, at irradiation. We also report for Bi–Al–Y–Si fiber notable radiation-induced changes in the photo-bleaching behavior of the centers throughout the VIS/NIR range. Another point deserving attention is that the Stokes shift of the cutoff wavelength after irradiation is insignificant (∼25 nm at the maximal dose) in this type of fiber.</jats:p>
